markdown_report:
**Recommendation:** retain matched-target prefix-removal training in the supplied corrected GRU4Rec. At 10% progress, controlled identification remains preferable to learned retention; no validation improvement is established.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Latest padding probes pass in all categories, with state errors below 7.1×10⁻⁷ and unchanged probe rankings. This supports tested layouts under diagnostic precision, not universal or deployment invariance. (2) Electronics has 8.25% wrong-rank positions and 19.81% margins below 0.5. These describe sampled training weaknesses, not harmful older context. (3) Feedback motivates testing recency. Ownership, compatibility and immediate intent remain unobserved.

**Insights from related work.** (1) FCESR and Demystifying Sequential Recommendations distinguish recommendation dependence from predictive usefulness [1,2]. Deletion effects alone cannot establish harm. (2) TimeSHAP and history-shuffling studies support temporal interventions [3,4]. Frozen-model sensitivity differs from training augmentation. (3) Recurrent augmentation, CL4SRec and recency dropout establish substantial precedent [9–12]. Endpoint-preserving, matched-supervision controls are the contribution. (4) Sampled metrics and random-denominator estimators require careful interpretation [5,6]. Neither training margins nor normalized suffix losses identify full-catalog performance.

The directions remain trustworthy encoding, controlled context intervention and ranking-aware diagnosis. The framework separates context, supervision and weighting:

| Condition | Training context | Supervised positions | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Full | All valid | Baseline |
| B | Full | Sampled suffix | Retention-weighting control |
| C | Same sampled suffix | Identical to B | Context intervention |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Matched-target prefix removal [1–3,9–12] | 4/7/6 | Separates context from supervision | Familiar augmentation; demanding matching |
| Frozen prefix/recent/random deletion audit [1–4] | 3/6/3 | Cheap dependence comparison | Perturbations create atypical histories |
| Jointly learned GRU forgetting gate | 4/6/7 | Adaptive retention within one network | Existing GRU gates already forget; adds confounds |

**Selected algorithm.** With probability 0.5, draw K uniformly from ceil(n/2)…n; otherwise K=n. Retain the final K real positions and their original next-item labels. B/C share masks, negatives, initialization and schedules; B preserves prefix gradients. For a decomposable baseline objective, both use the same retained-position mean.

```text
sample baseline batch and candidate pool
construct suffix mask with independent crop RNG
context = cropped input for C; full input for A/B
supervision = all valid for A; retained valid for B/C
update one GRU with the declared baseline loss reduction
```

Position t has inclusion probability pₜ=½+½·count{k≥max(ceil(n/2),n−t+1)}/count{k≥ceil(n/2)}. Expected normalized weights are E[Iₜ/M], not pₜ/E[M]. Thus B−A includes recency weighting and normalization; B does not shorten context. C−B tests context removal under matched supervision, without identifying stale intent. IPW cannot reconstruct full-context losses after cropping.

Use full-history inference, final-nonpadding readout and matching deployment precision. Complete twelve category fits only if affordable; select one complete condition by macro validation HR@10 without fusion. Preserve seeds, routing, diagnostics and predictor consistency. Record all queries and training-only frequency/length audits to expose selection optimism and possible shortcuts. References appear in related_work.

idea.description: Test stochastic old-prefix removal in the supplied corrected GRU4Rec using a matched-target full-context control with explicitly characterized target weighting. Execute each condition as a separate trial with one independently trained model per category, and deploy one complete selected condition with exactly one checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: The latest supplied diagnostics pass padding calibration in all four categories with both TF32 flags disabled. Repeating extensive numerical debugging is unnecessary unless new failures appear, but deployment must use and verify the declared precision policy. Qualitative feedback motivates a recency hypothesis, while sampled training margins—particularly Electronics' 8.25% wrong-rank rate—do not establish harmful older context or validation gains. At 10% progress, distinguishing context removal from altered supervision and target weighting is more informative than introducing learned selectors. Cropping and recurrent forgetting have established precedents; the proposed contribution is experimental identification.
idea.implementation_notes:
Integrate into the host-supplied corrected baseline; its architecture, sampler and objective are not supplied here and must not be reconstructed from assumptions. Retain the GRU4Rec backbone and any jointly trained baseline readout. A uses full context and all valid supervision; B uses full context with suffix supervision; C removes the prefix and uses exactly B's supervision. Preserve connected gradients through B's prefix. B−A contains no input-context shortening: it measures the combined training effects of altered supervision, recency weighting, normalization and any resulting regularization balance. C−B measures the specified context-training intervention under matched supervision, rather than a causal mechanism of stale interest.

For each nonempty row, let n be its real-input count and m=max(1,ceil(n/2)). With probability 0.5 draw K uniformly from the inclusive integers m through n; otherwise K=n. Retain the final K real-input positions, with singleton rows unchanged. Actual removal probability is below 0.5 because K=n is allowed. Preserve original aligned positive and negative targets; never reconnect targets across deleted positions. Keep inference on all permitted history within the baseline's unchanged maximum length. A causal unidirectional GRU must prevent a position's next-item target from appearing in its input prefix, even when that item appears at a later teacher-forced position.

For position t indexed 1 through n from oldest to newest, p_t=0.5+0.5*[n-max(m,n-t+1)+1]/(n-m+1). This expression concerns real-input retention; eligibility for the actual baseline loss must additionally be recorded. With retained-position mean loss and M retained valid positions across the batch, the coefficient is E[I_t/M], not p_t/E[M]. If every real position is eligible, an isolated row has exact coefficient 0.5/n + 0.5/(n-m+1)*sum_{k=max(m,n-t+1)}^n(1/k). Variable eligibility and batch composition require the corresponding actual denominator. Consequently, matching target identities alone does not match A's objective weighting. This is an explicit property of B/C, not a nuisance silently removed from the experiment.

Do not add inverse-probability weighting to the primary A/B/C experiment. For a decomposable, fixed full-context loss, I_t/p_t with a fixed full-valid-position denominator would recover that loss mean in expectation conditional on the batch. Normalizing by the random sum of inverse weights instead gives a generally finite-sample-biased ratio estimator. Cropping changes recurrent features and losses, so neither weighting scheme recovers A's full-context losses in C. Any IPW control would be a separately declared, separately budgeted follow-up, not an interpretation applied retrospectively.

Match B/C initialization, base batches, crop plans, candidate IDs, multiplicities, filtering and sampling corrections using independent deterministic RNG streams. Use stable category identifiers and explicit category/epoch/batch/row keys or recorded crop plans; do not use process-randomized hashes. Construct coupled candidate pools before supervision masking, and retain A's pool construction wherever compatible with its actual baseline semantics. Identical seeds alone do not prove matching. Preserve the actual objective's semantics: use a retained-position mean only where the baseline objective admits that decomposition, match positionwise regularization, and retain global regularization. Do not introduce sampling corrections or additional negative-count normalization. If negatives or normalizers couple positions, explicitly define and record which candidate pool is held fixed and how masked query losses are reduced before implementation. Handle empty supervised batches identically and record actual updates. Different recurrent execution paths may still change dropout masks; do not claim identical stochastic trajectories.

Use the existing successful precision protocol as a bounded regression check, preserving its declared tolerances and restoring temporary diagnostic settings afterward. Retain abs(error)<=1e-5+1.3e-6*abs(reference) and the separate absolute-only 1e-5 state criterion; do not relax them retrospectively. Record versions, dtype, device, both TF32 permissions, repeated-call error, layout differences, score errors and top-10 membership versus ordering changes separately. Existing passing measurements were obtained with both TF32 flags disabled. Declare that same policy for training, artifact reload and the generated predictor, and recheck the actual deployment path; restoring a temporary diagnostic setting does not define production precision. TF32 permission does not establish kernel use, disabling it does not guarantee bitwise equality, and seed 42 does not by itself ensure CUDA determinism. Preserve or explicitly document baseline deterministic-algorithm and CUDA workspace settings consistently across conditions; do not introduce unequal execution policies. Small shape-dependent differences alone do not identify a padding or checkpoint defect.

Do not infer universal invariance from the supplied small probe. Compact chronological real tokens before any packed recurrence, restore batch order and aligned B×L×H features, and gather the greatest nonpadding position rather than count-1. Define empty-history behavior explicitly. Retain the independent promoted-weight FP64 recurrence as a bounded troubleshooting reference if failures recur, including all recurrent layers and baseline readout transforms. It is a numerical reference, not exact arithmetic or proof of semantics. Verify finite outputs, independent-example state resets and gradients when modifying encoding.

Predeclare a common epoch count no greater than 200, exactly 200 batches per epoch, final-epoch checkpoints, validation-query cap, precision-check limits and timing allocation. Respect the SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200 despite its name. All twelve category-condition fits, diagnostics and failures share the remaining allocation from the original 43,200 GPU-second budget; do not assume the full original budget remains. Four slots do not multiply it. Use host-exposed accounting to establish affordability before committing to the comparison. If affordability is unknown or insufficient, report the comparison as incomplete rather than claiming matched evidence. Each separate trial trains only its chosen condition's four category models on one GPU. Never inspect other trials or reuse their checkpoints. The host may compare explicitly returned aggregate results across conditions without sharing their trained artifacts.

Select one complete condition using equal-weight macro validation HR@10; predeclare exact ties as A, then B, then C. Preserve the pinned evaluator: 200 validation users/category, 99 unique negative candidates and evaluation seed 42. Report C−B and B−A separately, with all category scores, retained-supervision counts, empirical inclusion rates by lag, candidate-pool summaries, update counts and charged time. Matching B/C masks yields matching nominal target weights and denominators when validity is defined from the original batch; never recompute loss eligibility from C in a way that silently changes these controls. Random cropping still changes C's contexts and gradients. No superiority or held-out improvement is currently established.

If host-exposed per-user validation hits are available, use 10,000 paired within-category user-bootstrap replicates with an analysis-only seed-42 RNG, shared resampling indices across conditions, equal category weights and 95% percentile intervals for B−A and C−B. Retain fixed candidate sets and report hit/miss transitions. If only aggregate scores are exposed, mark paired intervals unavailable. One changed hit equals 0.5 percentage points of category HR and 0.125 percentage points of macro HR. These exploratory intervals condition on fitted checkpoints and fixed candidates; they exclude training-seed and candidate-resampling variability and do not correct adaptive selection or multiplicity. Record every validation query and condition result rather than presenting only the winner.

Predeclare descriptive item-frequency and user-history-length bands from training histories, with boundaries, tie handling and counts recorded before outcome comparisons. Use exposed validation target identities and per-user hits for subgroup summaries only when available; otherwise mark those summaries unavailable. Supplement with fixed causal training-prefix audits, excluding each target from its input and defining eligible catalog competitors explicitly. Label any full-catalog HR@10, target-rank or margin audits as training measurements, separate from the host selection metric. Compare history-length and popularity bands to detect concentration of gains; neither popularity concentration nor lower embedding alignment alone proves shortcut learning or better diversity. Cropping may emphasize recent transitions or popular items, and full-history inference retains a train–inference context mismatch. Gains would support this augmentation policy, not establish immediate intent or elimination of stale interests.

Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four routes for Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), family-specific sample_batch and every ModelView interface: actual trained model, item_emb, log2feats, predict_score, user_train, meta_data and review_data. Accept (None, sequence, positive, negative) with B×L tensors; restore model mode and temporary diagnostic settings even on failure. Return measured metrics plus definitions, counts and explicitly unavailable unsupported values. The interpretation prompt must include measurements and definitions and distinguish observations from hypotheses. Use only permitted histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps. Unavailable ratings, review text, item categories, prices, stores, ownership, compatibility and simulator traits must remain unavailable despite generic dataset examples. Preserve unseen-item full-catalog recommendations for twenty real training users, five per category.

Update the predictor writer whenever inference or numerical settings change. Strictly reload the saved architecture and exactly one checkpoint per category, call eval(), and compare generated-predictor preprocessing, item mappings, aligned features, final readout and candidate scores against the training-side model on identical histories under the deployment precision policy. Do not average checkpoints, mix category winners across conditions or combine independently fitted scores. No ensembles, separately fitted popularity or transition components, or additional pretrained data are introduced. The code has not been executed or evaluated in this writing call.

Keep frozen deletion audits as a low-cost alternative or supplement within a declared diagnostic allocation. Learned retention is a later possibility after controlled evidence; it must be assessed against the GRU's existing gates and remain jointly trained within one network. Deterministic truncation, interior crops, input dropout, contrastive losses and IPW controls are not silently added to this twelve-fit design. Any later comparison must specify target identities, causal label alignment, supervision weighting, candidate pools, optimizer updates and inference history limits. Interior crops require their actual following targets or an explicitly different prediction horizon. CL4SRec supplies representation-level contrastive views, not permission to reuse an arbitrary endpoint label.
idea.pseudocode:
Predeclare A/B/C, crop probability 0.5, common E<=200,
200 batches/epoch, final checkpoints, query cap, tie order A/B/C,
deployment precision policy, diagnostic limits and charged budget.
Freeze training-only popularity/history-length bands and audit probes.
Check affordability of twelve category-condition fits using remaining host accounting.

For each separately executed condition:
  For each required category:
    initialize supplied corrected GRU4Rec with training seed 42
    initialize reproducible independent base-sampling and crop streams
    apply the same declared numerical policy to training and predictor generation
    For epoch in range(E):
      For batch_index in range(200):
        _, x, positive, negative = family_specific_sample_batch(...)
        candidates = baseline_candidate_pool_before_masking(...)
        valid = baseline_valid_supervision(x, positive, negative)
        keep = false mask shaped like x
        For each nonempty row:
          positions = chronological nonpadding positions of original x
          n = number of positions
          m = max(1, ceil(n/2))
          K = n
          if independent_crop_rng.random() < 0.5:
            K = uniform_integer_inclusive(m, n)
          keep[row, positions[-K:]] = True
          record theoretical p_t and empirical retention by lag
        # Reproduce exact B/C base batches, candidates and crop plans.
        context = x.masked_fill(~keep, 0) if condition == C else x
        supervision = valid if condition == A else valid & keep
        # Validity comes from the original batch for both B and C.
        # B keeps full prefix-to-suffix gradient paths.
        features = model.log2feats(context)
        loss = actual_baseline_objective(
            features, original_targets, fixed_candidates,
            supervision, predeclared_objective_specific_reduction)
        # For an already decomposable valid-position mean:
        # B/C loss = sum(supervision * position_loss) / sum(supervision).
        # Preserve global regularization and match positionwise regularization.
        # Do not add IPW, new sampling corrections or negative-count division.
        handle empty supervision identically in B/C
        update using baseline optimizer and schedule
        log retained valid counts, actual updates, candidate summaries and cost
    save final checkpoint and matching predictor artifacts
    strictly reload one checkpoint into its exact architecture
    verify finite outputs, state resets, padding alignment and empty histories
    read greatest nonpadding index in original coordinates, never count-1
    compare training-side and generated-predictor features/scores
      on identical inputs under actual deployment precision
    run bounded declared regression diagnostics; restore temporary settings
  obtain unchanged host four-category macro validation HR@10
  retain per-user hits and target identities only if host exposes them

Report B-A as supervision/weighting/normalization effects with full context.
Report C-B as the matched-supervision context-training intervention.
Report only completed comparisons, all queries, category scores and charged cost.
If paired hits are exposed:
  bootstrap paired users within categories 10000 times, analysis seed 42
  report differences, 95% percentile intervals and hit/miss transitions
Else:
  mark paired intervals unavailable
Report predeclared shortcut strata only where supporting data are available.
Keep causal training-prefix catalog audits separate from validation results.
Select one complete condition by macro HR@10; exact ties prefer A/B/C.
Deploy full-history inference within the unchanged maximum length,
with exactly one checkpoint/category and no fusion.
Preserve the diagnosis adapter and every ModelView interface.
Do not claim stale intent, full-catalog generalization or held-out gains.

originality.positive: Matched suffix supervision, explicit random-denominator weighting and fixed candidate construction make a familiar cropping intervention more interpretable.
originality.negative: History deletion, recurrent input augmentation, temporal attribution and controlled ablations have substantial precedent; this is primarily an experimental design contribution.

future_potential.positive: Can establish whether context interventions merit adaptive forgetting within a single GRU and provide reusable controls for sequence augmentation.
future_potential.negative: Benefits remain unmeasured; context mismatch, sampled evaluation, adaptive selection and a single training seed limit broader conclusions.

code_difficulty.positive: Preserves the supplied backbone and inference history policy, using input and supervision masks as the main learning changes.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact coupled-candidate matching, objective-specific reductions, RNG isolation, deployment precision consistency and a budgeted twelve-fit comparison make the complete protocol more demanding than the previous score of 5.

related_work.title: Demystifying Sequential Recommendations (2025)
contributions: As described in the supplied search results, studies minimal history edits that change recommendations.
Motivates intervention-based analysis of recommendation dependence.
limitations: Recommendation changes under history edits do not establish predictive harm or user intent.
Does not establish efficacy of the proposed GRU4Rec training augmentation.

related_work.title: FCESR (2025)
contributions: Distinguishes retained-history sufficiency from removed-history necessity.
Provides a conceptual basis for separating context-preservation and deletion probes.
limitations: Explanation properties do not directly identify the best training context policy.
Deletion effects depend on perturbation construction.

related_work.title: TimeSHAP
contributions: Provides recurrent-model temporal attribution and prefix-pruning methods.
Supports investigating contributions of older sequence events.
limitations: Attribution is not causal evidence of latent intent.
Does not establish that stochastic prefix removal improves held-out ranking.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential? (RecSys 2024)
contributions: Includes inference-time history-shuffling probes for trained GRU4Rec models.
Motivates testing dependence on chronological structure.
limitations: Small shuffle effects may reflect dataset structure rather than a model defect.
Frozen-model perturbations and training-time augmentation answer different questions.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Establishes that sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog metrics, including model ordering.
Supports limiting conclusions to the pinned candidate-set benchmark.
limitations: Does not justify modifying the mandated evaluator.
Does not determine which context intervention will improve this benchmark.

related_work.title: The Self-Normalized Estimator for Counterfactual Learning
contributions: Provides background on objectives containing random normalization denominators.
Motivates distinguishing expected ratios from ratios of expectations when interpreting retained-position losses.
limitations: The suffix-retention coefficients in this report are direct derivations, not results established for GRU4Rec by this paper.
Counterfactual estimators do not restore recurrent contexts altered by cropping.

related_work.title: Adaptive Normalization for Inverse Probability Weighting
contributions: Provides background on normalization choices for inverse-probability estimators.
Supports distinguishing fixed-denominator weighting from self-normalized ratio estimation.
limitations: Weighting recovers an unchanged loss objective only under the relevant sampling and positivity conditions.
Does not justify treating cropped-context losses as full-context losses.

related_work.title: PyTorch 2.5.1 Numerical Accuracy
contributions: Documents floating-point differences between mathematically equivalent batched and individual computations.
Supports tolerance-based comparison under recorded execution settings.
limitations: Provides no GRU-specific universal error bound.
Numerical agreement on finite probes does not prove semantic correctness.

related_work.title: Improved Recurrent Neural Networks for Session-based Recommendations — Tan et al. (2016)
contributions: Uses session-prefix training and embedding dropout for recurrent recommendation.
Provides direct precedent for recurrent sequence augmentation.
limitations: Prefix expansion differs from deleting an old prefix while preserving endpoints and aligned targets.
An all-position GRU baseline may already supervise the same next-item transitions.

related_work.title: Recurrent Neural Networks with Top-k Gains for Session-based Recommendations
contributions: Provides GRU4Rec recurrent next-item training and ranking-loss precedents.
Motivates preserving the actual baseline's negative sampling and loss normalization.
limitations: The supplied corrected implementation cannot be assumed to reproduce every official GRU4Rec detail.
Does not establish a benefit from old-prefix removal.

related_work.title: Contrastive Learning for Sequential Recommendation — CL4SRec
contributions: Uses cropping, masking and reordering to construct contrastive sequence views.
Establishes substantial precedent for sequence augmentation.
limitations: Contrastive crops need not preserve the original endpoint or next-item label.
Representation-level supervision differs from the proposed matched-position recommendation loss.

related_work.title: Recency Dropout for Recurrent Recommendation
contributions: As described in the supplied search results, provides a recurrent augmentation precedent that reduces dependence on recent interactions.
limitations: Its intervention direction and motivation differ from discarding old context.
Does not establish that greater recency emphasis is appropriate for these four datasets.

related_work.title: PyTorch 2.5.1 CUDA Semantics
contributions: Documents separate CUDA matmul and cuDNN TF32 permission controls.
Identifies recurrent modules among operations affected by cuDNN precision settings.
limitations: Permission to use TF32 does not prove that a particular kernel used it.
Disabling TF32 does not guarantee equality across batch shapes.

related_work.title: PyTorch 2.5.1 Reproducibility
contributions: Distinguishes random seeding from deterministic execution controls.
Documents additional CUDA reproducibility settings.
limitations: Deterministic execution does not guarantee identical results across different computation shapes or environments.
Execution controls cannot replace explicit matching of samples, candidates and crop plans.
